beats.beat: A B Infrabuild operates in two segments: creation of infrastructure and operating a ready-mix concrete (RMC) plant.

The company wins contracts through a competitive bidding process. Clients issue tenders, pre-bid meetings are held, and the lowest bidder gets the job. The contractor must deposit a performance guarantee.
Its main services cover railways (designing platforms, gauge conversion, track laying), bridges (various types), and roads (bituminous and concrete).

Major clients include Western Railway, Central Railway, Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM), Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation (MRVCL), and Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA).
Revenue is heavily concentrated: top clients contributed 57% of total revenue in fiscal 2018, and Western Railway alone accounted for 52% of the order book.
The company has been working with Western Railway since 2006 and operates primarily in Mumbai and Maharashtra.

business.heading: What the company does
business.purpose: Explain the business model: tender-driven government contracting, two segments, key clients, and the order book dependency on Western Railway.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations fell from ₹90.21 crore in fiscal 2015 to ₹60.53 crore in fiscal 2018.
Net profit after adjustments was volatile: ₹0.96 crore in fiscal 2014, then dipped to ₹0.16 crore in fiscal 2017, before jumping to ₹3.15 crore in fiscal 2018.
EBITDA (Profit before Interest, Depreciation and Tax) ranged from ₹7.84 crore (FY2014) to ₹9.29 crore (FY2018), with a low of ₹6.76 crore in FY2017.
Short-term borrowings increased from ₹30.82 crore in fiscal 2014 to ₹35.37 crore in fiscal 2018, while long-term borrowings decreased from ₹5.87 crore to ₹1.33 crore over the same period.
Total assets grew from ₹70.62 crore in fiscal 2014 to ₹82.32 crore in fiscal 2018.
The company has reported negative cash flows in recent years, which could affect operations if sustained.

financials.heading: Financials
financials.purpose: Present a multi-year financial narrative using the restated statements: revenue, profit, EBITDA, debt, and assets. Highlight key trends.

beats.beat: The company is promoted by Amit Bholanath Mishra, who holds 74,95,476 equity shares – 90.949% of the pre-issue capital.
Other directors hold only 300 shares each. The CFO is Anchal Pachori (CA) and the Company Secretary is Mohit Soni (ACS).

The company has engaged in related-party transactions: loans taken from KMP/Board of Directors ₹68.4 lakhs in FY2018, director remuneration ₹57.7 lakhs, and outstanding payables of ₹324.3 lakhs as of March 31, 2018.
Two companies promoted by the promoter – Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited – were struck off by the Registrar of Companies in March 2016 due to non-operation.
The company has not appointed an independent agency to appraise the project, nor a monitoring agency to oversee fund deployment. Funds will be deployed at management discretion.

beats.beat: The infrastructure sector contributes about 8% to India's GDP. It is highly fragmented and working-capital intensive, with both organized and unorganized players.
Growth drivers include government programs such as the 100 Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, Make in India, and Power for All. Eased FDI norms in 15 sectors also support growth.
India needs an estimated ₹50 trillion (US$ 777.73 billion) in infrastructure investment by 2022 for sustainable development.
The industry faces headwinds: slow pace of government projects, changes in government policies, and working capital crunches that can affect profitability.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild Limited builds infrastructure — railways, bridges, roads — and also runs a ready-mix concrete plant. Almost all its revenue comes from government clients in and around Mumbai.
The company is offering 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each in a fresh issue to raise funds primarily for working capital. The issue price is yet to be determined.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: A B Infrabuild is an infrastructure construction company focused on government contracts in Mumbai, now raising working capital via an SME IPO.

beats.beat: The IPO is a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of face value ₹10 each. There is no offer-for-sale component; all shares are new.
The lead manager is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited. The registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.
Proceeds from the fresh issue will be used for: (1) meeting working capital requirements of ₹1,130 Lakhs, and (2) general corporate purposes (amount not disclosed).

offer.heading: The offer
offer.purpose: Detail the issue structure: fresh issue only, size, lead manager, objects of the issue.

beats.beat: Customer concentration: Western Railway alone accounted for 52% of the order book and top clients for 57% of revenue in FY2018. Losing this client would severely impact revenue.
Dependence on government tenders: the company's revenues rely on winning bids from government and PSU projects. If bids fail or are negotiated lower, financial performance suffers.
Negative cash flows: the company has experienced negative cash flows in recent years, which could impair working capital and operations.

Related-party transactions and unsecured debt: as of March 31, 2018, the company had ₹405.02 lakhs in unsecured loans repayable on demand, and significant related-party payables. A sudden demand could strain liquidity.
Governance concerns: two promoter-held companies were struck off, and the IPO lacks an independent project appraisal or monitoring agency for fund use.

beats.beat: The DRHP provides key financial ratios for the company: EPS of ₹12.39, NAV per share of ₹44.71, and RoNW of 28.14% for fiscal 2018. The face value is ₹10 per share.
The issue price is yet to be determined. The filing states that the price will be justified based on the accounting ratios, but no peer comparison with named companies is provided in the digest.
